entries.claim: The z statistic for a mean is (x-bar - mu0)/(sigma/sqrt(n)) and requires a known population sigma
entries.notes: Large-sample z is a close approximation to t

entries.claim: When sigma is unknown the t distribution is used; Gosset published it under the pseudonym Student
entries.notes: t has heavier tails; df depends on design

entries.claim: Paired designs analyse within-unit differences rather than two independent groups
entries.notes: Ignoring pairing loses power and misstates the standard error

entries.claim: The chi-square statistic sums (observed - expected)^2/expected and requires adequate expected counts
entries.notes: Cochran rule of thumb: expected counts about 5 or more

entries.claim: The F ratio compares sample variances but is sensitive to non-normality; Levene and Browne-Forsythe are more robust
entries.notes: scipy ttest_ind with equal_var=False uses Welch degrees of freedom

entries.claim: With k independent comparisons at level alpha the family-wise error rate is approximately 1-(1-alpha)^k, giving about 14.3% for k=3, alpha=0.05
entries.notes: Exact under independence; positive dependence lowers the true rate
